parameters.note: How many imported sessions the phone sends in one request (K-609, K-615): the contract's WorkoutImport maxItems and the server's keel.training.import.max-workouts, kept equal by ImportLimitsMirrorTests. Small enough that one request stays quick on a slow connection, large enough that a year of sessions (~200) is ten requests.

The most sets of one session the phone sends (K-609): the contract's ImportedWorkout.sets maxItems and the server's keel.training.import.max-sets, kept equal by ImportLimitsMirrorTests. A real session is far under it; past it the first ones go and the rest are counted as left out.

How alike a file's move name must be to a catalog name or alias to be offered for it (K-609): the share of words the two have in common (Dice: twice the shared words over both counts). 0.5 offers 'Squat (Dumbbell)' the barbell squat (one of two words) and nothing that shares no word. Never a match by itself: only a name whose words are the catalog's exactly is matched without the user (U5).
How many catalog moves are offered for a name not matched (K-609): one tap each; more is a list to read, and 'Other' opens the whole catalog.

The program draft (K-957, ADR-073 Ek 1) reads the sessions of this many weeks, ending on the day of the file's last session (not today: an export made a while ago still shows its last program). A month shows a weekly program four times and an alternating one twice; older sessions are not today's program.
A named session done at least this often in the window is a day of the draft (K-957). Once is a one-off (a quick arm day, a try), not a day of the program.
A move with working sets in at least this share of its routine's sessions is part of the day (K-957); less is a swap or a one-off.

A routine is as many days as it was done a week (K-957), each on a weekday it fell on in at least this share of the weeks it was done, the largest shares first: Upper on Monday and Thursday is two days. Weekdays tied at that count, or too few, leave a day without one, and the user places it (once a week on Monday and Thursday in turn is one day). Two days wanting one weekday: the larger share keeps it, the other stays without one.

The draft's rep range is where the middle share of the move's working sets fell (K-957), the interquartile range at 0.5: a light set Strong does not mark as a warm-up (H13 B2), or one bad last set, does not stretch it.

The draft's rep range is at least this wide (K-957), opened at the top: double progression needs room to climb (K-109), and the reps seen stay the bottom, so the first session's load does not jump. Always 8 becomes 8-10.
